# Copilot instructions -- ACF Terraform modules

Generic conventions for every `terraform-aws-acf-*` module. Apply unless a
module's own `README.md` explicitly overrides a rule.

Reference layout and pipeline expectations:

- [acai-solutions/github-workflows/tree/main/docs](https://github.com/acai-solutions/github-workflows/tree/main/docs)
- [acai-solutions/github-workflows/tree/main/sample-terraform-module](https://github.com/acai-solutions/github-workflows/tree/main/sample-terraform-module)
- [acai-consulting/template-terraform-aws-module](https://github.com/acai-consulting/template-terraform-aws-module)

When unsure about file placement (`main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`,
`examples/<name>/`, `tests/terratest/<name>_test.go`), mirror the sample module.

## 1. `terraform {}` requirements block

Every `.tf` file that owns a `terraform {}` block uses **exactly** this shape:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"

  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = ">= 5.0"
    }
  }
}
```

- `>= 1.5.0` is the floor for both Terraform (1.5.7 = last MPL release) and
  OpenTofu (>= 1.6). Do not raise the floor without a concrete reason.
- Do **not** add `configuration_aliases = []`. Declare aliases only when the
  module actually receives a non-default provider configuration from its caller
  (e.g. `aws.audit`, `aws.logging`, `aws.target`). In that case extend
  `required_providers.aws` with `configuration_aliases = [aws.<name>, ...]`.
- Do not pin patch versions; use `>=` ranges so consumers stay in control.
- Additional providers (e.g. `awscc`, `time`, `random`) follow the same shape:
  `source` + `>= MAJOR.MINOR`, no patch pin.

## 2. Variable validations

- Put `validation {}` blocks **only on the outermost module's variables** -- the
  surface the user actually fills in (top-level module `variables.tf` and
  `examples/*/variables.tf`).
- Do **not** repeat the same validations on nested / internal modules. The
  outer layer already guarantees the contract; duplicate checks add noise and
  drift risk.
- Boundary rule: validate at the system boundary (user input, external APIs).
  Trust internal callers.
- Prefer one focused validation per concern with a clear `error_message` over
  one big `alltrue([...])` expression.

## 3. Module structure

- Reusable modules contain **no provider blocks** -- only `required_providers`
  with `configuration_aliases` when needed. Provider configuration lives in
  `examples/*/provider.tf` (and any caller-side aliases file such as
  `*_roles.tf`).
- Standard files at module root: `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`,
  `README.md`, `LICENSE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. No `terraform.tfvars` at the root.
- Tags: merge `var.resource_tags` with the standard ACAI module tags
  (`module_provider = "ACAI GmbH"`, `module_name`, `module_source`,
  `module_version`) inside the module via a `locals { resource_tags = merge(...) }`,
  and assign `tags = local.resource_tags` on every taggable resource.
- Outputs are stable contracts -- name them by intent, not by implementation
  detail, and never expose internal-only values.

## 4. Examples

- Every module ships at least one runnable example under `examples/`. The
  canonical one is `examples/complete/` (or a numbered series for round-trip /
  scenario coverage).
- Each example owns: `backend.tf` (partial S3 backend), `provider.tf` (all
  `aws` providers + aliases the module needs), `variables.tf` (filled from
  `<TEST_BED>_TESTBED_TFVARS`), `main.tf` (`terraform {}` block + module
  instantiation with `source = "../../"`), `outputs.tf` (`test_success*`
  assertion outputs evaluating to the literal `true` on a healthy deployment).
- Add new examples in numbered, complexity-ordered sequence; never leave gaps
  after deletion -- renumber and update both READMEs.

## 5. Terratest

- Tests live in `tests/terratest/` as `<example>_test.go` with one
  `func Test<ExampleName>(t *testing.T)` per file.
- Use the shared helpers from `helpers_test.go` (per-test backend state key,
  `TERRATEST_TERRAFORM_BINARY` switch, warning-stripping output readers).
- Assertions read `test_success*` outputs and compare to the string
  `"true"`. Do not destroy in-test on failure -- the workflow handles cleanup.
- `go.mod` / `go.sum` are generated by the workflow on first run and need not
  be hand-edited.

## 6. Compatibility

- Both `terraform` (1.5.7) and `tofu` (>= 1.6) must pass `init -backend=false`,
  `validate`, and the Terratest suite.
- Avoid BSL-licensed Terraform features (>= 1.6) and OpenTofu-only features.
- Keys passed into `for_each` / `count` must be plan-time-known. Never derive
  them from unknown resource attributes.

## 7. Style and discipline

- Don't add comments that restate the code. Keep a comment only when the *why*
  is non-obvious (a hidden constraint, a workaround, an invariant).
- Don't add error handling, fallbacks, or feature flags for cases that cannot
  happen given the module's contract.
- Don't refactor, rename, or "improve" code outside the scope of the requested
  change.
- Prefer small, composable submodules over one mega-module with conditional
  feature flags.
- README structure follows the sample module: purpose, usage snippet, inputs,
  outputs, examples table, links.

## 8. Security

- Never hard-code account IDs, ARNs, KMS keys, or role names. Take them as
  variables.
- IAM policies follow least-privilege: scope by resource ARN and condition
  keys (`aws:PrincipalOrgID`, `aws:SourceAccount`, etc.) -- no `Resource = "*"`
  without an accompanying condition.
- Encrypt at rest by default (`kms_key_arn` variable, default `null` =
  AWS-managed key). Allow the caller to inject a CMK.
